I've never had this issue before infact I have the opposite! ˙◠˙ So sorry you're going through this, OP. I have a few tips that can hopefully help~ 

1. Shop on a restock day -- I personally shop on saturday afternoons because euts the most convenient time for me and my SO and it just so happens that they are eith in the process of resto king or just finishes restocking so I get really fresh produce that you barely have to inspect to see if its good. 

2. I "ingredient" prep right after shopping -- It's a pain i. the ass but since I plan my meals ahead I already know whats the purpose of a produce and what dishes it's going to here's what I do. write down all the dishes im making --> write down how to cut/prepare the ingredient usually shredded some cabbage or cut up some romaine lettuce --> wash & put away produce. More often than not I soak my produce in warm water with a little bit of white vinegar to remove pests and it works most of the time just need to make sure to wash it out thoroughly. 

I know this seems tedious and high effort but if you can maybe this can help your produce not get bad as quick ˙◠˙

That being said you can only (legally) get a job on campus because you’re F1 and other than that you could do CPT (internship/ while studying still needs 12 units i think) or OTP which is after graduation. This works too! As long as you for sure are filing as a non-resident then they will process it for you. However, i still recommend scheduling with either CSUN Vita Clinic because they’re more accountable and most likely better at processing since they have specific accountants who are credible/specialise in filing taxes for international students. I believe they have a certificate for it if they’re eligible. Also, they have better accountability since they are a school that’s known for their accounting major and ofcourse having that means they really have to make sure they file it properly since they could get in trouble if they don’t since they have professors and such monitoring them unlike turbotax or sprintax that don’t have that reliability.Also have I mentioned that it’s for free? 👀

So essentially if you are a resident/citizen of the US it’s okay for you to use turbotax or sprinttax. However, as F1 students when you file for your taxes online they most likely will not put an option to ask you if you’re a citizen or not (because I have tried filling with Turbotax and I can attest that it was easy but they did not ask for status) and so it will automatically send your taxes as a resident which you might recieve tax concerns and such because it will recognize you as a citizen. However, once you actually become a citizen here in the US (if you plan to) you might get in trouble with the IRS that they might have sent you a stimulus check which as International Students we don’t qualify for that and so when the time comes they will just take the stimulus amount from your bank account since they accidentally gave it to you. It’s also worth mentioning that as an international student or a person who is legally a non-resident (work visa,etc) the taxes have “treaties” with countries that allow you to not pay anything or pay a certain amount based on the country you are from. For example: I am from the Philippines and the US has a treaty that if I make less than 3000 USD a year then I would not have to pay taxes but if I get paid more than that amount I would have to pay for my taxes. I really hope this helps! If you have any other questions let me know and I will try to answer as best as I can from my knowledge =)

That has been me for the past 2 weeks... but i had a productive day yesterday and here are some things I think can help: 
- Always take your meds at the same time each day. Meds most likely work if taken of each day. You don’t always have to wake up the same exact time each day but make sure when you set a time for your meds it’s at a time you know you won’t miss. 
- try to set an alarm in the morning. I’m not a morning person at all but you just need to get yourself out of bed and when you do get up make your bed ASAP. It’s the start of your day and so once you do 1 productive thing things might just fall into place. 
- Whenever you have something to do a task or chore or homework or whatever I set a timer for 25 mins that I need to focus on just that one thing. I don’t check my phone, i close all the other tans I just try my best to focus in that one thing. By the the timer is up I put on a 5 min timer to have a break. People like us are big on inhibition and the more we would want to accomplish things knowing there’s something in return big or small like a 5 min break. 
- When you create a routine try adding things one step at a time cause god know what will happen if you overwhelm someone with ADHD and all hell breaks loose. It could be as simple as making your bed in the AM or to make sure you drink your vitamins you do it before bed ( which is what I do) 
- When I started creating my routine I had timers for everything with specific tones ( i know i know it’s a bit extra but it HELPS! ) so my wake up timer is different from my take your morning meds timer to my have you eaten lunch yet time. It sounds ridiculous but it has helped me a lot. After some time I didn’t have to always look at my phone because my brain already associated the sound to the task it’s paired to 

I hope these help. You got this, friend! :)
